artists.biography:
No-Man are an English art-pop duo formed in 1987 as No Man Is An Island (Except The Isle Of Man) by singer Tim Bowness and multi-instrumentalist Steven Wilson (the latter also of Porcupine Tree). The band has so far produced six studio albums and a number of singles/outtakes collections (most notably, 2006's career retrospective, All The Blue Changes). The band was once lauded as "conceivably the most important English group since The Smiths" by Melody Maker music newspaper.
Originally creating a sample-based proto-trip hop/ambient/electro-pop-styled music, No-Man has pursued a more organic, diverse and band-oriented sound in subsequent years. Drawing from a diverse mix of singer-songwriter, post rock, minimalist, progressive rock, jazz and contemporary ambient sources for inspiration, No-Man's musical style is distinctive yet difficult to categorise.

perplexity.description:
Scatter - Lost Not Lost Volume Two (1991-1997) is a remastered and expanded 2026 edition of No-Man's 1999 official bootleg Lost Songs CDR, released on Burning Shed and featuring material recorded between 1991 and 1997. This compilation captures the duo of Tim Bowness and Steven Wilson at their most adventurous and eclectic peak, blending genres like electronic, rock, and pop into a dynamic 61-minute collection of dissonant Art Rock experiments, sweeter-than-sweet melodies, corrupted grooves, vicious intensities, graceful flourishes, epic expanses, and concise bursts. Guest appearances from luminaries such as Robert Fripp, Mel Collins, Theo Travis, and Colin Edwin add layers of progressive sophistication, highlighting No-Man's boundary-pushing ethos during their early years.

The tracklist spans 15 cuts, including standout pieces like "Gothgirl Killer" (6:22), "All the Reasons" (5:16), "Samaritan Snare" (4:56), "The Night Sky" (6:36), and "Coming Through Slaughter" (5:25), which exemplify the band's genre-defying range from abrasive noise to ethereal beauty. Packaged in a digifile CD format, this release not only revives rare archival material that influenced the founding of Burning Shed in 2001 but also underscores No-Man's critical acclaim—once dubbed "conceivably the most important band since the Smiths" by Melody Maker in 1990—as innovative architects of atmospheric, experimental soundscapes.

Its significance lies in documenting a fertile creative period for No-Man, bridging their art-pop roots with prog and ambient explorations, and offering fans deeper insight into the unreleased gems that shaped their evolution, all while receiving praise for its bold remastering and eclectic vitality.
